subtasks.title: Write tests for serve package (server, auth, handlers)
subtasks.description: Create test files for the internal/serve package covering: (1) auth_test.go — bearer token middleware rejects missing/invalid tokens, accepts valid token using constant-time compare, returns 401 with JSON error body; (2) handlers_test.go — GET /api/health returns 200 with JSON status, GET /api/agents returns agent dashboard rows with unread counts (wire testutil.NewTestStore + testutil factories); (3) serve_test.go — server starts and stops cleanly, ListenAddr defaults. Create stub files (serve.go, auth.go, handlers.go) with minimal types/function signatures so tests compile but fail. Tests use net/http/httptest for handler tests. Auth tests verify crypto/subtle constant-time comparison indirectly (correct token passes, wrong token fails, empty token fails). Agent handler tests create agents via store.CreateAgent and messages via store.CreateMessage, then verify JSON response shape.

module_boundaries.description: HTTP bridge server with auth middleware and agent dashboard API — stubs only for test compilation

subtasks.title: Implement serve package (server, auth, handlers)
subtasks.description: Implement internal/serve/ package to make all pre-written tests pass: (1) serve.go — Server struct holding Config and *csuite.Store, New() constructor, ListenAndServe(ctx) that wires mux with auth middleware and graceful shutdown via context; Config struct with ListenAddr and BearerToken fields. (2) auth.go — BearerAuth middleware using crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, returns 401 JSON on failure, skips auth for /api/health. (3) handlers.go — HealthHandler returns {"status":"ok"}, AgentsHandler calls store.AgentDashboard() and returns JSON array with agent name, status, unread_count, and latest_inbox fields. All handlers set Content-Type: application/json. Do NOT modify the pre-written tests.

subtasks.title: Write tests for serve subcommand and config
subtasks.description: Create tests in cmd/csuite-watcher/main_test.go (or a new serve-specific test section) for: (1) serveTomlConfig parsing from [serve] TOML section — verify listen_addr, bearer_token, db_path fields parse correctly; missing file returns zero-value config; (2) serve subcommand dispatches correctly from the run() switch — unknown subcommand still errors, 'serve' is recognized. The test for the subcommand switch can verify that run(["serve", ...]) does not return the 'unknown subcommand' exit path.

subtasks.title: Implement serve subcommand and config wiring
subtasks.description: Wire the serve subcommand into cmd/csuite-watcher/main.go: (1) Add serveTomlConfig struct with ListenAddr, BearerToken, DBPath fields following watcherTomlConfig pattern. (2) Add Serve field to dremToml struct for [serve] TOML section. (3) Add loadServeConfig function following loadWatcherConfig pattern. (4) Add 'serve' case to the subcommand switch in run(). (6) Add [serve] section to drem.toml with listen_addr, bearer_token, db_path defaults. (7) Add nhooyr.io/websocket dependency to go.mod (go get). Update usage strings to include 'serve'. subtasks.title: Integration: end-to-end serve subcommand verification and docs
subtasks.description: Final integration subtask: (1) Verify all tests pass with `go test ./internal/serve/... ./cmd/csuite-watcher/...`. (2) Verify `go vet ./...` passes. (3) Verify `gofmt -l` shows no unformatted files. (4) Verify file length and function count ceilings (800 lines, 20 exported functions). (5) Verify internal import ceiling (serve package should import only csuite — 1 internal import, well under ceiling of 6). (6) Run constitution check if available. (7) Update README or docs with serve subcommand usage if user-facing documentation exists. This subtask ensures the serve skeleton works end-to-end: config loads, server starts, auth rejects bad tokens, health endpoint responds, agents endpoint returns dashboard data. No unit tests here — integration verification only.

assumptions.decision: Adding serve subcommand to existing csuite-watcher binary rather than creating a new cmd/bridge-server binary
assumptions.why_chosen: Task description explicitly says 'Add serve case to cmd/csuite-watcher/main.go subcommand switch' — this is specified, not inferred.

assumptions.decision: Health endpoint is unauthenticated (no bearer token required)
alternatives: Require bearer token for all endpoints including health
assumptions.why_chosen: Health checks are typically unauthenticated for load balancer probes and monitoring. The middleware can skip /api/health. This is a standard HTTP server convention.

assumptions.decision: JSON response shape for agents endpoint uses snake_case field names (name, status, unread_count, latest_inbox)
assumptions.why_chosen: snake_case is the conventional JSON naming for REST APIs and matches the TOML config field naming convention used throughout the project.

alternatives: Additional fields like read_timeout, write_timeout, cors_origins
assumptions.why_chosen: Minimal config for a skeleton server. Task description specifies following watcherTomlConfig pattern which has only essential fields. Additional config can be added when needed.

assumptions.decision: Server.ListenAndServe takes a context.Context for graceful shutdown rather than separate Start/Stop methods
assumptions.why_chosen: Context-driven shutdown matches the runWatcher pattern which uses signal.NotifyContext and passes ctx to the runner. Single method is simpler and deeper.

assumptions.decision: nhooyr.io/websocket added to go.mod but not used in code yet (skeleton only)
alternatives: Skip websocket dependency until actually needed
assumptions.why_chosen: Task description explicitly requires adding nhooyr.io/websocket dependency. It prepares for future WebSocket upgrade of the bridge server.
